newsitem.title: USA: Morgan Stanley, Dean Witter debt tighter on merger.
newsitem.headline: Morgan Stanley, Dean Witter debt tighter on merger.

text.p: The debt of Morgan Stanley Group Inc and Dean Witter, Discover & Co tightened following news the companies agreed to merge, high-grade traders said on Wednesday.
"The companies' bonds are a few basis points tighter across the board on the news," said one corporate finance trader.
Traders noted that neither company has much debt outstanding.
"The debt tightened a couple of basis points ... there's not going to be a huge change in either paper because they're both comparably rated," said one corporate finance trader.
Dean Witter bonds due 2006 tightened from a 62 basis points bid to trade at a 60 bid, high-grade traders said.

The new company, which will be called Morgan Stanley, Dean Witter, Discover & Co, will be a leader in the securities and credit services businesses ceating a financial giant with market capitalization of $21.0 billion.
On Wednesday, credit rating agency Moody's Investors Service Inc said it may raise the A1 senior debt rating of Morgan Stanley as well as the A2 senior debt rating of Dean Witter, Discover & Co.
Standard & Poor's later affirmed the A-plus senior debt rating of Morgan Stanley, and said it may raise the single-A senior debt rating of Dean Witter.
In early New York Stock Exchange trade, Morgan Stanley shares soared 7-3/4 to 65-1/8 and Dean Witter shares added 1-3/4 to 40-3/8.
